entries.input: Let $\phi(x, y)$ satisfy $|\phi(x, y_2) - \phi(x, y_1)| \leq A |y_2 - y_1|$. Then the initial value problem $y' = \phi(x, y)$, $y(a) = c$ has at most one solution on $[a, b]$.
entries.name: LipschitzUniquenessForInitialValueProblem
entries.binders: (φ : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) (a b c A : ℝ) (hL : ∀ x y₁ y₂, |φ x y₂ - φ x y₁| ≤ A * |y₂ - y₁|) (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt f (φ x (f x)) x) (hg : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt g (φ x (g x)) x) (hfa : f a = c) (hga : g a = c)
entries.conclusion: ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, f x = g x
entries.title: Uniqueness for Lipschitz initial value problems
entries.witness: ⟨fun _ _ => 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, fun x y₁ y₂ => by simp, fun _ => 0, fun _ => 0, fun x _ => hasDerivAt_const x 0, fun x _ => hasDerivAt_const x 0, rfl, rfl, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $\phi$ be a continuous bounded real function on the strip $0 \leq x \leq 1$, $y \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the initial value problem $y' = \phi(x, y)$, $y(0) = c$ has a solution on $[0, 1]$.
entries.name: PeanoExistenceTheorem
entries.binders: (φ : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) (hc : Continuous (Function.uncurry φ)) (hb : ∃ M, ∀ x y, |φ x y| ≤ M) (c : ℝ)
entries.conclusion: ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, f 0 = c ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, HasDerivAt f (φ x (f x)) x
entries.title: Peano existence theorem
entries.witness: ⟨fun _ _ => 0, continuous_const, ⟨0, fun x y => by simp⟩, 0, trivial⟩
